reviews.review: Great game.  Story was good.  Can't wait for the next mass effect game.

Highly enjoyable. I know when it came out it had a lot of heat for the differences between it and the trilogy, but I enjoyed it so much. I've played even more hours on my play station. The romance isn't all that, but it's never been all that in the Mass Effect worlds (Though it feels like the purpose to me sometimes). It gives me the same thrills that the Trilogy did while keeping the story line different and introducing a new story line away from the trilogy without ruining the story. I enjoyed and would recommend a play through if you enjoyed the world of Mass Effect.

Good game, still a bit buggy for me, not too big a deal. I bought this at 8 bucks, good value at that price. Combat fun, story fun even though the choices don't really have much weight. They influence some things (i think literally one thing), but hopefully choices made will impact any future game, like we so loved in the ME trilogy. 

Vetra best girl.

So here it goes, the unavoidable comparison, the bad and the really good. 

Comparison: I get why this game has received a bad reputation. It's not like the trilogy where every single mission was exciting, the charachters were really well written, and you actually cared about their survival and friendship. I remember the decissions in the trilogy were life and death and Shepard was a bad ass whose relationships felt important. You got a sense of urgency, loss, wonder and relevance that Andromeda  lacks. But, to be fair, it was a really high standard to achieve and many of us are unfair nostalgia wise. Mostly because it's a sequel to an amazing trilogy (regardless of your opinions about the end).

The bad: the game was rushed. You can tell from the Asari models that they all share the same face. The charachter customization sucks. Some story aspects could have been explored with more substance. The fact that so many species were not implement in upcoming DLCs, (where are my quarians?!), etc. Also, you don't get the same feelings you could get in the trilogy in the relationships with your crew. Some substance in the writing is indeed lacking. All of this could probably be atributed to EA wanting microstransactions in the multiplayer, their complete disregard for having creativity and taking risks and due to the downsizing in the amazing team that brought ME trilogy to life. There is also the infamous Direct X bug that randomly happens and that nobody has really pinpointed it or solved. But my major issue is on the script. Andromeda is a new galaxy and things feel pretty milky wayee. Every single andromeda species and planet could also be in the Milky Way. I would have gone bonkers with the writing there. A subplot about microrganisms, fungus or something like in the expanse or other idea so weird that transported you to another realm. A language in feelings or senses, something different! I mean, there is so much you can do! But instead, the remmnant feels  like the protheans, the kett sound like the geth (lazy writting) and they behave like the collectors. They use guns and ships exactly like in the Milky Way. Point is, writters could have played more with a new galaxy (but probably couldn't thanks to EA and the payment cuts, and all that). Also, why get rid of the paragon/renegade dynamics? Finally, the decissions don't carry much weight. So, why play this?

The good: I enjoyed the combat (but play it on maximum difficulty otherwise it's too easy), I enjoyed some of the charachters, the point of having a protagonist that learns on the job and who is younger. I enjoyed the exploration and some interactions with the crew, though probaly could have used more crew members and flings, and more inner conflict (I do enjoy my drama). The story is not bad, derivative but not bad. Some missions are a lot of fun. But that's it, it's fun, not special. So, really if you have EA pass or miss the trilogy, give it a chance, judge for yourself. It still has some  good stuff that keeps you intrigued. Haven't finished it but until now, veredict is: a 6.9 out of 10. Will update once I finish it. Thanks for reading!

Update: the ending is very anticlimatic, so it's a 6/10. No real conflict. Again, they could've gone bonkers with the twist of chapter 9. Nothing happens, Nothing is in danger. There are no consequences. It's fun but it's not ME.
